none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references: - Ahmed Khaled and Peter Richtárik. [Better Theory for SGD in the Nonconvex World](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.03329v3). 2020 (preprint v3). Complexity: $O\!\left(1+\frac{L\Delta}{\varepsilon^2}\max\left\{1+B,\frac{A\Delta}{\varepsilon^2},\frac{C}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}\right)$ stochastic-gradient oracle calls with a fixed budget, using SGD, for $\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_{\mathrm{out}})\|\le\varepsilon$.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objectives on a second-countable real Hilbert space E. The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz, L>0. A finite infimum fstar exists, need not be attained, and f(x0)-fstar≤Δ with Δ≥0. Convexity is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AbcNoiseNonconvex.lean: Params; spec.valid; spec.admissible gradient, smoothness, infimum, and initial-gap conditions.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns g(x,ω) using a fresh IID sample. The jointly measurable oracle is unbiased: E[g(x,ω)]=∇f(x). Gradient replies are integrable and centered squared errors are integrable. One call supplies one gradient estimate; function values and same-sample paired evaluations are not supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AbcNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.admissible IID, oracle answer, measurability, unbiasedness, and integrability conditions; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: ABC variance model: E‖g(x,ω)-∇f(x)‖²≤2A(f(x)-fstar)+B‖∇f(x)‖²+C for every x, with A,B,C≥0. This permits variance to grow with the objective gap and gradient norm; no uniform variance bound or exponential-tail condition is imposed. Equivalently, E‖g(x,ω)‖²≤2A(f(x)-fstar)+(1+B)‖∇f(x)‖²+C. All Params, including L,A,B,C,Δ,ε,x0, are public; fstar and the oracle distribution are existential instance data.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AbcNoiseNonconvex.lean: Params; spec.Public; spec.publicInput; spec.valid; spec.admissible variance inequality and existential witnesses.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The output is a point in E satisfying E‖∇f(output)‖≤ε, ε>0. The criterion uses the first power of the norm. The output must be measurable and its gradient norm integrable; no last-iterate requirement is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The gradient-norm bound averages over the joint law of algorithm randomness and IID oracle randomness, under a fixed cap on oracle calls.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AbcNoiseNonconvex.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence, executeWithTrace, and _run.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth nonconvex stochastic optimization with unbiased IID gradients, the established ABC variance condition, and expected first-order stationarity is a standard formulation. The Hilbert-space ambient setting broadens the usual finite-dimensional statement.
